ops-bot: ALERT: increased token-stream stalls detected for us-west2-pool (streaming_latency > 95th pct) at 2026-02-02T14:12:25Z
Carla H: seeing intermittent stalls in streaming responses — clients report long pauses mid-token. started ~14:05 UTC, affects ~6% of requests to model-x-large in us-west2.
Carla H: logs show repeated gRPC deadline exceeded and a lot of retransmits. sample stack: 
```
GRPC stream error: deadline exceeded
stream chunk delayed 0.3s -> 1.2s -> 0.05s
transport_status: UNAVAILABLE, retryable=true
```
Vikram S: thanks, tagging in. Any node-level change this afternoon? kernel or nic driver patch rolled? :thinking:
Jen (sre): I just checked node kube events — we deployed kernel-5.15.90-hotfix on the us-west2-gpu pool at 13:58. also saw a flurry of netlink MTU updates during the rollout.
Carla H: that smells like MTU mismatch / GRO/GSO weirdness. streaming is sensitive to reordering/jitter. can we get tcpdump on an affected pod?
Jen (sre): grabbed a snippet from host capturing egress/ingress around 14:06:
```
14:06:21.123456 IP a.b.c.d.12345 > x.y.z.80: Flags [.], seq 12345:12589, ack 9876, win 64240, length 244
14:06:21.123567 IP x.y.z.80 > a.b.c.d.12345: Flags [.], seq 9876, ack 12589, win 32768, length 0 (duplicate ack)
14:06:21.124012 IP a.b.c.d.12345 > x.y.z.80: Flags [.], seq 12589:12840, ack 9876, win 64240, length 251 (out-of-order)
14:06:21.124412 IP x.y.z.80 > a.b.c.d.12345: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0, length 0
```
Jen (sre): counts show spikes in dup acks and RTOs for a subset of flows.
Vikram S: that aligns w/ the kernel NIC driver change. Some drivers changed offload/GRO semantics -> different packet coalescing, which can reorder segments on certain topologies. also worth verifying RDMA configs on nodes with Mellanox adapters.
Mike G: can anyone confirm if RDMA enabled on those instances? last I checked, us-west2-gpu has mixed NICs (mellanox + intel) after capacity add. mixed NICs + different firmware can cause reorder.
Jen (sre): ran quick checks: `rdma link show` returns devices on 8/12 nodes, `ethtool -k` shows GRO/TSO enabled on all, but tx-checksum varies. MTU is 9000 on some hosts and 1500 on others.
Carla H: MTU mismatch! that explains fragmentation and reassembly jitter. streaming token responses are small but rely on low-latency ACKs; reordering from path MTU differences can inject small delays that accumulate.
Vikram S: quick mitigation options: 1) pin model traffic to nodes with homogeneous NICs via nodeAffinity / taints; 2) temporarily set node `net.ipv4.tcp_congestion_control` to a less aggressive algo on affected nodes; 3) force MTU to 9000 OR 1500 cluster-wide (we prefer cluster-wide consistency).
Mike G: immediate short-term: increase gRPC per-stream deadline by 300ms and enable streaming-alive-heartbeat to mask small stalls. Long-term: normalize MTU and firmware rollback for NIC driver that introduced the change.
Carla H: we should also consider adding per-request fallback to a compatible model variant in other AZ if deadlines start failing >5% — cheaper to failover than drop tokens for customers.
Jen (sre): taking action: 1) pin new deployments away from mixed-nic nodes (daemonset label update) — started 14:30 UTC; 2) collect full tcpdump for packet reassembly traces and will upload to central logs (link: https://dash.redwood.internal/logs/streams/1775012345).
Vikram S: I'll open infra ticket to roll NIC firmware if needed and coordinate with cloud provider. tagging oncall: @Mike G can you validate the gRPC deadline bump config in staging?
Mike G: will validate now. staging config tweak: `GRPC_STREAM_DEADLINE_MS=1200 -> 1500` and enable `STREAM_HEARTBEAT_MS=200`. will roll to canary in 10m.
Carla H: thanks — once canary looks good we'll roll to us-west2. Jen, please post postmortem stub and timeline after we stabilize.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-02-02-1879 by Jen (sre) — label: network-reorder, severity: high. link: https://incidents.redwood.internal/INC-2026-02-02-1879
Jen (sre): updating incident with pcap and node list. action items: normalize MTU cluster-wide (owner: Vikram), validate firmware (owner: Vikram), lifecycle: canary tweak -> rollout (owner: Mike), postmortem (owner: Carla).
Carla H: tagging customer-success to notify impacted customers if we cross SLA threshold. good catch everyone. :thumbsup:
